mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) contraction of more than 1% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is simultaneously falling signals a supply-side shock that raises costs without improving labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -1% AND UNRATE direction is up
regime_hint: supply shock during labor market recovery
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% within a quarter signals an emergency easing response to a financial crisis, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% within a quarter after being above 2% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails outside of crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE direction is up AND PAYEMS direction is up
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 1% while the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is flat signals improved supply without inflationary pressure, which supports corporate margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of rising oil prices.
